To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the best fingerprint-based methods for virtual screening are the binary kernel discrimination method, the extended Tanimoto coefficient, and data fusion of individual similarity rankings.

(1) the binary kernel discrimination method is the most accurate method for fingerprint-based similarity searches; (2) the best method for fusing similarity scores from different fingerprints is a simple linear combination of scores; (3) the best method of combining similarity scores from different similarity searches is a simple weighted linear combination of scores, with the weights being the inverse of the number of reference structures in each search; and (4) substructural analysis methods are not competitive with other methods

(1) fingerprint-based methods for virtual screening are most effective when multiple bioactive structures are available; (2) the best approach for combining multiple bioactive reference molecules is data fusion, in which the similarity scores from individual searches are combined using an appropriate weighting scheme; (3) the most effective data fusion method is binary kernel discrimination; (4) the best individual method for virtual screening is binary kernel discrimination, followed by the extended connectivity fingerprint and the topological torsion fingerprint.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (i) How can we use multiple reference structures in fingerprint-based similarity searching? (ii) What is the effect of the choice of fingerprint? (iii) What is the relative performance of different fingerprint-based methods for similarity searching?
the problem of comparing the results of similarity searching using multiple bioactive reference compounds.
the development of methods for virtual screening using multiple bioactive reference molecules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best method is data fusion, but that the best individual method varies from dataset to dataset.
the best approach is to use the best method for each particular case, and that there are no general rules for selecting the best method.

the best approach to virtual screening using multiple bioactive reference compounds depends on the particular database and query set, and that the most effective approach may not necessarily be the one that is most conceptually straightforward.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the best results are obtained from the binary kernel discriminant method.
the best fingerprinting technique for a given dataset depends on the dataset, the similarity measure, and the application.

if the goal of a virtual screening exercise is to identify the most active compounds from a large database, then the binary kernel discrimination method should be used, and if the goal is to identify the best lead compounds, then the combined fingerprint should be used.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of fingerprinting technique and similarity measure is critical for virtual screening.
, for the purposes of virtual screening, the best fingerprint-based method is the one that gives the best results for a given dataset.
, for virtual screening, there is no single best fingerprint, and that the choice of fingerprint should be based on the nature of the data and the goals of the search.
